text: Continuum. The runtime stops. The mission continues. When an agent process dies mid-mission, in-memory context dies with it. Continuum makes the recovery boundary visible.
Production agents fail while tools are running and work is half complete. Restarting from zero can duplicate side effects. Asking a human to explain the mission again defeats autonomy.

Invocation A checkpoints the cursor and event trail in CockroachDB Cloud on AWS. Amazon Bedrock Titan creates normalized vectors for the distributed vector index. The development agent inspects that same cluster through Managed MCP, on a separate read-only plane.

Now the live jury proof. One click creates a real mission and deterministically stops Invocation A after the second committed step. The request ends. Steps three and four remain pending in CockroachDB.
This console is not pre-rendered. The task cursor, event count, provider metadata, and recalled memories all came back from this client-scoped CockroachDB session. The provider evidence is Bedrock.

Resume starts a fresh HTTP invocation. Invocation B receives only the session UUID, reconstructs the mission from durable state, skips the two completed tasks, and continues at step three. No in-memory handoff. No human re-brief.
The same mission now shows four of four steps committed. Closing memory is written back with a Bedrock embedding and remains queryable beside the transactional state.

The public proof is client-scoped and rate-limited. Cross-site API calls are rejected, concurrent resume requests are atomically claimed, internal errors stay private, and secrets live only in platform bindings.
Continuum. CockroachDB for agentic memory. Bedrock for embeddings. Managed MCP for safe inspection. Built so agents survive failure. Memory is the product.
